inputs.cash_note: Cash, cash equivalents and investments at 2026-09-30 per Q3-26 10-Q balance sheet: cash 2,978.1 + short-term investments 1,064.4 + long-term investments 2,757.9 = 6,800.4 (10-Q MD&A: $6.80bn, down from $9.03bn at FY2025 on $4.4bn of repurchases and a $519m distributor acquisition). Investment-grade debt securities are counted as cash because the interest they earn is stripped from the flows (matching-asset rule). No borrowings. The $450m antitrust settlement was accrued but NOT yet paid at 2026-09-30 (litigation accruals 463.2), so it is deducted separately in the equity bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K: share-based compensation expense 802.8 (AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense; cash-flow add-back is 788.2) + taxes paid related to net share settlement of equity awards 419.1 (financing activities). ISRG publishes no combined SBC-plus-award-tax figure, so the two lines are summed per house method. Proceeds from stock plans (ESPP/option exercises, 350.3 in FY2025) are NOT netted against the charge.
inputs.interest_income_source: FY2025 10-K 'Interest and other income, net' (NonoperatingIncomeExpense) 365.9; 9M-2026 was 243.6 (9M-2025 274.6), falling as buybacks shrank the cash pile. The line is almost entirely interest on the cash-and-investments pile, which is added back at the end of the DCF, so it is stripped from the FCF base to avoid counting the pile twice.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases 2,295.3 (cash, financing activities); 9M-2026 a further 4,419.2 (11.0m shares, of which 7.8m / 2,939.8 in Q3 alone). Shares issued and outstanding fell 355.1m -> 346.6m between FY2025 and 2026-09-30. ISRG is an active repurchaser, so the flat share count is funded rather than a modelling convention.
inputs.share_count_basis: Period-end fully diluted estimate at 2026-09-30: 346.6m shares issued and outstanding (Q3-26 10-Q balance sheet) + 2.6m dilutive securities (Q3 weighted diluted 351.6 less weighted basic 349.0) = 349.2m. The period-end count is used rather than the Q3 weighted-average diluted 351.6 because the cash anchor is already net of the full $2.94bn spent on the 7.8m shares bought in Q3; using the weighted count would charge the cash without crediting the retired shares. Held FLAT because SBC (including award taxes) is fully expensed in the flows; charging dilution as well would double-count.
inputs.price_note: Regular-session close per Yahoo Finance chart API (regularMarketTime); not an after-hours print.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD discount rate. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST), ERP ~5%, equity beta ~1.0-1.2 for a large-cap no-debt medtech gives a cost of equity of 9-10%; with zero debt WACC = cost of equity. 9.0% used, held identical across all three scenarios so that risk is charged once, through the probability weights, not twice through a per-scenario rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment A: operating leases (liability $171m at FY2025, immaterial against $8.6bn of cash) stay inside operating expenses/EBITDA; lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt. Systems ISRG places with customers under operating leases are ISRG's own PP&E funded through inventory (an OCF working-capital outflow), which is why the working-capital capture is strongly negative.
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated flows include the Intuitive-Fosun China JV; NCI earned 20.6 of FY2025 net income (11.2 in 9M-2026, down from 15.9 as China placements slowed; book NCI 131.6 at 2026-09-30). Deducted once, in the equity bridge, at ~15x FY2025 NCI earnings (310) rather than at book, so the flows stay consolidated and the minority is charged at a market-like value. Left unchanged: at ~15x the lower 2026 run-rate it would be ~225, a difference of $0.25/share.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 1: US operating company), UNCHANGED from the 2026-09-29 build. ISRG is a single-segment razor/razor-blade operating business (instruments and accessories ~60% of revenue, systems ~25%, service ~15%) with no debt and positive free cash flow; none of the non-FCF routes apply and none of the owner-fcf-adaptations are material. THIS IS AN UPDATE (see reconciliation). Anchors refreshed to the Q3-26 10-Q (2026-09-30): cash and investments 8,625.5 -> 6,800.4, period-end diluted shares 357.3 -> 349.2, and the accrued-but-unpaid $450m antitrust class settlement added to the equity bridge after tax (347). Drivers re-judged on Q3-26 evidence: (1) year-1 growth 17.5% -> 19.5% (9M revenue +21.0%, Q3 +21.7% incl. the Italy/Spain/Portugal distributor acquisition; Q4 assumed ~+16% on a 2,866 comp with EUP 2.0 and China charge-code cuts starting); (2) years 2-4 growth cut 2.0/1.0/0.5pp for the guided 3-5% mix-constant decline in I&A revenue per procedure through 2027 (I&A is 60% of revenue), US procedure growth slowing to 10% in Q3 (FY2026 procedure guide narrowed to 14-15%), lapping the distributor acquisition, and Ottava's August 2026 de novo authorisation; (3) EBITDA margin: year 1 raised to 47.0% (9M pre-SBC EBITDA ex the litigation charge was 47.7%, flattered by one-off IEEPA tariff refunds), years 2-3 held at 46.0% as the price cuts land and refunds do not repeat, mature level lowered 48.0% -> 47.5%; (4) SBC incl. award taxes re-anchored 11.5% -> 10.5% of revenue (9M SBC expense 641.8 + award taxes 378.5 = 11.7% of 9M revenue, but award taxes are ~93% paid in Q1, so the full year lands near 10.4%), mature 8.0% unchanged; (5) D&A re-anchored 6.2% -> 7.4% (9M depreciation 559.0 + amortisation 85.0 = 7.4% of revenue; management guides both to keep rising) fading to 6.5%; (6) PP&E capex year 1 5.5% -> 4.0% (9M 329.0 = 3.8%), returning to 5.0% by year 4; (7) working-capital capture -50% -> -55% (9M operating assets and liabilities used 532.5 AFTER a ~450 litigation accrual inflow, i.e. ~-980 underlying on a 1,513 revenue increase = -65%; ~-54% excluding the 168 prepaid-tax build); (8) weights 20/50/30 -> 25/50/25. DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: FY0 = FY2025 and the owner-FCF base 902.9; WACC 9.0% in every scenario (would move on a sustained shift in the 10y UST, not on company news); terminal growth 3.0/3.0/2.5 and the 20x cap; cash-tax path 20% -> 22% (9M prepaid taxes rose on accelerated R&D deductions, a timing benefit that is not perpetuated; a durable change in ISRG's non-GAAP ETR guide of ~22-23% would move it); base growth years 5-10 (10/9/8/7/6/5), which would move on evidence of Hugo/Ottava taking measurable US placement share or of EUP 2.0 lifting benign-procedure volumes; the 10-year horizon; the NCI deduction. Owner FCF FY2025 = 2,490.7 - 1,221.9 - 365.9 = 902.9 (9.0% of revenue) versus a 24.7% reported FCF margin. The litigation settlement is a one-off: it is excluded from the margin path and charged once in the bridge. Separate antitrust suits from independent service companies are unquantified and sit in the bear narrative and weight, not in the bridge.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 12.9% vs revenue 5yr 18.2% (-29%) and EPS 5yr 21.5% (-40%): equity growth is depressed by $4.6bn of buybacks in FY2022 and FY2025, so book value understates the compounding rate. Year-1 growth in the scenarios is anchored to FY2026 guidance and H1-26 actuals, not to this figure; the 12.9% is the forward proxy for screening only.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs are FY2022->FY2025 (3yr) and FY2020->FY2025 (5yr) on the Metrics CSV. Owner-FCF CAGRs use the SBC-, award-tax- and interest-adjusted series above, which was ~zero in FY2023-24 during the facilities capex supercycle (capex 1,064 and 1,111 vs 540 in FY2025); the 60.6% 3yr owner-FCF CAGR is off a trough and is not a usable anchor. SBC+award taxes grew 26%/yr FY2020-25 (574 -> 1,222) against reported FCF growth of 17%: an increasing share of reported cash growth is being paid for in stock and withholding cash.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 19.5%: 9M revenue +21.0% (Q3 +21.7%, helped by the acquired Italy/Spain/Portugal distribution businesses and 546 placements); Q4 assumed ~+16% against a 2,866 comp as EUP 2.0 and the November China charge-code cuts begin. FY2027 11.5%: da Vinci procedures ~12-13% (US running 10%, OUS 20%) less ~2pp from the guided 3-5% mix-constant fall in I&A revenue per procedure on 60% of revenue, and the acquisition lapping. Years 3-4 trimmed 1.0/0.5pp as the pricing phase completes; years 5-10 (10 -> 5%) unchanged from the prior build. Ten-year average ~9.7%.
base.margin_rationale: Adjusted EBITDA (pre-SBC, pre-D&A) was 43.3% in FY2025 and 47.7% for 9M-2026 excluding the $450m litigation charge (2,419.8 + 450.0 + 641.8 + 559.0 + 85.0 on 8,711.8), flattered by IEEPA tariff refunds booked against cost of revenue. Year 1 47.0%. Years 2-3 step back to 46.0% as the I&A price cuts land (worth ~2-3% of revenue gross before volume response) and refunds do not repeat; recovery to 47.5% mature on da Vinci 5 mix and opex leverage, 0.5pp below the prior 48% because the pricing concession is competitively driven and unlikely to be reversed.
base.sbc_rationale: FY2026 lands near 10.4%: 9M SBC expense 641.8 + award taxes 378.5 (93% of FY2025's award taxes were paid in Q1, so Q4 adds little) + ~216 of Q4 expense on ~12.0bn revenue. SBC expense alone is ~7.2% of revenue; the withholding-tax component moves with the share price and is lower after the 2026 de-rating. Declines ~0.3pp/yr to 8% mature (unchanged end point).
base.wc_rationale: -55% of the change in revenue: FY2024-25 ran -65/-75% (lease-fleet build via inventory, receivables); 9M-26 ran ~-65% underlying once the ~450 litigation accrual is removed from the 532.5 reported use, ~-54% also excluding a 168 prepaid-tax build. Modelled on growth so the drag fades as growth decelerates.
base.tax_rationale: UNCHANGED. Cash taxes 537.9 in FY2025 = ~21% of engine EBIT. GAAP ETR 13% is flattered by excess SBC tax benefits that are not perpetuated; ramps to 22% (ISRG non-GAAP ETR guidance ~22-23%).

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 closes near +19.5% revenue with da Vinci procedures at the guided 14-15%. In 2027 the EUP 2.0 volume-based instrument pricing and China charge-code cuts take 3-5% off I&A revenue per procedure, US procedure growth stays near 10% (ACA subsidy expiry, GLP-1 bariatric softness) while OUS runs ~20%, and revenue growth steps down to ~11.5%. The da Vinci 5 replacement cycle (315 of 546 Q3 placements), cardiac and SP general-surgery indications and Ion (+31% procedures) keep growth at 10-11% through 2030 before Hugo and Ottava, both now authorised in the US, take share at the margin and growth fades to 5% by 2035. Adjusted EBITDA dips to 46% while the price cuts land and tariff refunds roll off, then recovers to 47.5%. SBC incl. award taxes glides from 10.5% to 8% of revenue. The $450m class settlement is paid once; no change to the service model is assumed.
scenario_narratives.bull: EUP 2.0 works as intended: lower instrument prices pull high-volume benign procedures (hernia, cholecystectomy) onto da Vinci faster than price falls, shutting Hugo and Ottava out of the mid-tier hospitals they need to reach scale. Procedure growth re-accelerates to mid-teens as ACA-related deferrals normalise, Ion and SP add second and third growth legs, and the new cardiac indication opens a ~160k-procedure pool. Revenue grows ~14% through 2029, da Vinci 5 mix and manufacturing scale lift adjusted EBITDA to ~51%, and SBC falls to 7% of revenue. The antitrust settlement closes the tying litigation without changes to the service/repair model.
scenario_narratives.bear: The price cuts turn out to be defensive rather than expansionary: per-procedure revenue falls 5% or more and keeps falling as hospitals use Hugo (US urology) and Ottava (US general surgery) as negotiating leverage, while US procedure growth settles in the high single digits because the ACA and GLP-1 effects are structural. China is largely ceded to domestic robots under the unified national pricing framework. The independent-repair antitrust suits succeed where the class action settled, forcing Intuitive to open EndoWrist reprocessing and third-party service, which erodes the instrument annuity. Revenue growth falls to 8% in 2027 and mid-single digits by 2029, adjusted EBITDA erodes to 42% while R&D must be sustained, SBC stays near 10% of revenue and the lease-fleet capital intensity does not fade. Terminal growth 2.5%. With $6.8bn of cash and no debt this is a value-compression case, not a solvency one.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from 20/50/30 to 25/50/25. Bear up to 25% because three things that were prospective in September are now facts: Ottava holds US de novo authorisation, management itself has cut instrument pricing 3-5% (pressure on the highest-margin, most recurring line), and a $450m settlement has put the service/instrument tying model in legal play with independent-repair suits still open. It stops at the bottom of the 25-35% band because ISRG has no debt, $6.8bn of cash and no going-concern or single-regulator exposure. Base stays 50% as the guided path. Bull down to 25% because it now also needs the pricing program to prove volume-elastic, on top of mid-teens procedure growth, margin expansion to 51% against two new entrants, and SBC compression to 7%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: House-basis owner-FCF DCF: SBC and net-share-settlement taxes are charged as cash costs, interest on the cash pile is stripped and the pile added back once, the share count is held flat, and the FCF margin is built from components so the FY2025 working-capital and capex troughs are neither perpetuated nor ignored. The street basis (SBC as non-cash) is reported alongside so the reader can see how much of the market price depends on that accounting choice.
key_risks_to_valuation: Competitive entry: Medtronic Hugo (US urology) and J&J Ottava (US de novo August 2026, general surgery) reaching scale would pressure system pricing and procedure share -- the bear axis.
Pricing: EUP 2.0 and China charge-code cuts take 3-5% off I&A revenue per procedure through 2027; whether volume responds decides between the bull and bear paths.

Antitrust: the $450m class settlement awaits court approval and independent service companies' suits continue; a forced opening of instrument reprocessing/repair would hit the annuity and is not in the base case.
US demand: procedure growth has slowed to ~10% (ACA subsidy expiry, GLP-1 bariatric declines); if structural, the base growth path is too high.
SBC treatment: house and street values differ materially because SBC plus award taxes run ~10-12% of revenue; the market price sits above even the street value.
Terminal-value dominance: a 10-year build leaves ~70% of value in the terminal; each 1pp of WACC moves value by roughly a fifth (see sensitivity grid).

Working-capital capture (-55% of revenue change) is the least-observed driver: the leased-fleet build sits in OCF as inventory, and if leasing mix keeps rising the drag could persist longer than modelled.
